steps.text: Beat eggs with lemon pepper and garlic pepper in a small bowl until blended. Stir together ground almonds and 1 cup Parmesan cheese in a shallow dish until combined.
Dust tilapia fillets with flour; shake off excess. Dip tilapia in beaten egg, then press into almond mixture to evenly coat.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook tilapia in melted butter until golden brown on both sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Reduce heat to medium, then season fillets with salt and sprinkle with remaining 1 cup Parmesan cheese. Cover and continue cooking until Parmesan cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.
Transfer tilapia fillets to a serving dish and garnish with parsley sprigs and lemon wedges.

raw_recipe.headline: Almond-Crusted Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: This almond-crusted tilapia is coated with egg, ground nuts, and Parmesan cheese for a quick and easy seafood dish that pairs well with any vegetable.

review.reviewBody: I've now made this a few times, I did add some lemon pepper to the dusting flour and use eggbeaters for the egg... this is perfect everytime, I've also used orange roughy with this also amazing. I do make a lot of the crust mixture and just put left over in the freezer for the next time. Oh, and I bake this instead of frying, I spray with pam and put in the oven at 425 or so and flip half way (time depending on how thick the fillets are) and spray again and put back in, perfect.

This is our favorite tilapia recipe and my husband LOVES it!! I use egg whites and bake it for 15-20 minutes at 425 degrees. You MUST bake it, so much better!! I have made this about 25 plus times. We eat this about every two weeks. Also, bake it on a cookie sheet with parchment paper and spray olive oil PAM on top of fishe before baking, no turning of fish needed.

This was a good tasting recipe, but I made a few changes that I think added a lot of flavor. I decided to add 3 TBs of olive oil to the butter. After the fish was done and removed, there were had some incredible drippings with pieces of almonds and the flavor from the parmesan and garlic, so I decided to make a roux. I added finely chopped green onions and a tsp of chicken bouillon then sautéd until the onions were translucent. I added a half cup of water and voilà! It was so savory!
I loved this recipe. Dipped the fish in flour, them egg, then crushed almonds then cooked in butter in an iron skillet. Served as a sandwich with mayo on toast. Simple and excellent.

A great starting point for a gluten-free recipe (just leave out the flour and no harm done)! I saw some reviewers state that it didn't have enough flavour and they liked the Broiled Tilapia recipe better. So....I combined both. Sort of. Here's what I did:
~ 1:1 ratio of almond flour to parm. (I used about a cup each)
~ 1/2 tsp dried basil
~ 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
~ 1/4 tsp-ish onion powder
~ 1/4 tsp celery seed
~ probably 1/2 tsp salt

I then cooked it as per the directions, using 2 eggs with salt for the first step (probably only needed 1). This was enough for 5 ocean perch fillets with about 1/3 cup of almond flour mix left. I wanted to make it into a hushpuppy type thing, but didn't get a chance.

We liked this fish and would make it again, but with few changes. I had some Flounder and that's what I used. 1st, I sprinkled the fillets with some salt and pepper. I kept the breading directions the same but fried in a mixture of butter and vegetable oil. 2 minutes per side was enough for the Flounder ( usually thinner than Tilapia). And, as another reviewer did, I omitted the step of adding more Parmesan cheese and further cooking of the fish. It would have made the delicate fish very dry.
I coarse chopped almond slivers instead of almond flour and it gave the end result such a good crunch. This was as yummy as it was pretty. Everyone at dinner tonight loved it. I will make it again!
Great recipe but always need to make more breading - at least 2xs more than original recipe calls for. Keep in mind. Other than that spot on.

Delicious and a definite keeper! I baked it in a foil covered baking dish and butter instead of frying it after I read some reviews that said it was a nice modification and it came out great! The whole house loved it!

This was delicious! Per the suggestions of other reviewers, I added the lemon pepper and garlic pepper to the flour. I also mixed the butter with Canola oil to avoid burning the butter. I only had 3 large filets and the parm/almond mix was the perfect amount. If you have more, you will definitely want to double. I finished with lemon and salt as well as the garnishes. Everyone loved it, and it is quite pretty on the plate! I will definitely make this again!

This had a very nice flavor but as another reviewer said, this should not have added Parmesan and extra cooking with the lid on. Makes what should be a nice crispy coating into a soggy mess. I'm not a huge parmesan fan so I used less in the mixture then called for. To me it was delicious that way. Also added a little olive oil to the butter so as not to have burnt butter flavor.
I have made this a couple times for my wife and I and we both love it as is! Definitely a keeper in the dinner rotation!
It was so good. My cat even loved. Lol. My hubby liked very much. Thank you!

I love this and make it twice a week. The only substitutes I made was to add lemon pepper to eggs, add the extra Parmesan as soon as I flipped the fillets. And fried in combo olive oil spray and butter.
I made fewer fillets, but the taste is just right.
Delicious and easy, but I left out parmesan.
Delicious. Substituted almonds for cashews (since I didn't have any). Served with sauteed spinach, and lemon parmesan spaghetti squash.

I was a little disappointed in the taste. I put it on a rack in the oven and maybe it didn't produce the same flavor as frying it in the skillet. I just didn't taste the almond flavor. I did add some toasted almonds on top at the end but the breading was flat. Maybe my almonds were too old.

This was terrific. I made very little alterations to it. I've used frozen Tilapia instead of fresh. Since I ran out of Parmesan cheese, I swapped it with bread crumbs in its place. I've grounded my own almonds to add for the crust. I skipped the lemon wedge and the parsley spring. I would love to make this again.
added less parmesan than the recipe
